newsitem.title: UK: LME may tighten regulations after Sumitomo scandal.
newsitem.headline: LME may tighten regulations after Sumitomo scandal.

text.p: The chairman of the London Metal Exchange (LME) hinted on Wednesday he would be ready to tighten regulations for the exchange in the wake of Japan's Sumitomo Corp copper scandal.

Raj Bagri said the LME was aiming to create the appropriate regulatory environment for all of its users, industrial and commercial, and was working with Britain's chief regulator the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) and other national and international regulatory agencies.

"We are always willing to make changes when necessary and we are looking forward with confidence to consulting with the SIB and the findings of its extensive consultation process and implementing with them...such enhancements as are deemed necessary," Bagri said at the annual LME reception.

"We truly believe that an appropriately controlled regulatory environment is in the best interests of all concerned," he added. "Inadequate regulation naturally creates concerns and the opportunities for wrongdoing."

The SIB as well as U.S. and Japanese regulators and fraud squads are making a global inquiry into events surrounding the dismissal on June 14 of Yasuo Hamanaka, head copper trader for Japan's metals conglomerate Sumitomo Corp.
Sumitomo alleges that Hamanaka was a maverick trader who ran up losses worth $2.6 billion in unauthorised deals. He was dismissed by Sumitomo in June.
SIB is also carrying out a wide-ranging review of the LME and will report its findings in December.

SIB chairman Sir Andrew Large said at the reception he hoped the SIB review and whatever happened as a result would ensure users' confidence in the future: "You can look forward to working in the markets you operate in with absolute confidence."

Earlier this week regulators from 17 countries met in London, agreeing a range of measures enhancing standards and best practice in contract design, market surveillance and information-sharing and cooperation on commodities markets.
